item.title: First Lady Melania Trump Announces 2026 Fall Garden Tours
item.description:

The White HouseSeptember 29, 2026
The White House will welcome visitors this fall for the 2026 Fall Garden Tours, offering an opportunity for visitors to experience the historic gardens and grounds of the People’s House. The grounds will be open Saturday, October 17 from 10:00 AM – 4:30 PM, and Sunday, October 18 from 10:00 AM – 2:30 PM.
Throughout the tour, guests will enjoy the beauty of the South Lawn, the Rose Garden, the White House Kitchen Garden, the expanded White House Beehive, and the new helipad. Rich in history and tradition, the White House gardens provide guests with a unique glimpse into the grounds that have served as a backdrop throughout our nation’s 250 years of history.
This event is free and open to the public. A ticket is required for all attendees, including small children. The National Park Service will distribute free, timed tickets at a tent outside the White House Visitor Center each day of the tours beginning at 8:30 AM. The White House Visitor Center is located at 1450 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, DC, 20004, near the intersection of 15th Street and E Street Northwest.
Tickets will be distributed—one ticket per person—on a first-come, first-served basis.
Please note the following items are not allowed on the White House grounds:
The Secret Service reserves the right to prohibit any other personal items. However, strollers, wheelchairs, umbrellas (no metal tips), and cameras are permitted. All items needed for medical purposes will be permitted on the tour (such as wheelchairs, electric scooters, glucose tablets, and EpiPens). Please identify and explain all items needed for medical purposes to Secret Service personnel upon arrival.
In the event of inclement weather, the event may be canceled. Please call the 24-hour information line at (202) 456-7040 to check on the status of the event. For more information, including what visitors will need to access the White House campus, please visitwww.WhiteHouse.gov/Visit.

item.title: Adobe, Amazon, Intel, Starlink, Google, and Zoom partner with First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together
item.description:
Office of the First LadyAdobe, Amazon, Intel, Starlink, Google, and Zoom partner with First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future TogetherThe White HouseSeptember 30, 2026

The White HouseSeptember 30, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump secured six new private-sector technology partnerships for Fostering the Future Together, including Adobe, Amazon, Intel, Starlink, Google, and Zoom.
“When I established Fostering the Future Together, the mission was clear: empower children through technology and education. Delivering on that mission demands alliances between best-in-class innovators and global leaders, especially as super intelligence transforms how the next generation learns,” said First Lady Melania Trump.
Combined, the new technology partners committed more than $23 million towards education, tools, and expertise, for children across the globe.
Google committed $4 million to expand its SI Educator Series globally through its new Fostering the Future Together partnership. “Google is proud to support First Lady Melania Trump’s vital effort,” said Google’s Maggie Johnson. “This investment demonstrates our belief in keeping educators in the lead.”
Intel will deploy its technology across ten countries through its SI for Citizens Program, SI for Youth Program, and Semiconductor Education Pathways Program. Adobe will provide students worldwide with free SI-powered study and creation tools through Student Spaces. Amazon will expand free access to its Kiro SI coding assistant, reaching 5 million students through 132 universities, while AWS Academy will provide free training to more than 2 million students. Zoom Cares will provide $2.75 million in SI for Good grants across Europe, Africa, Latin America, and the Asia-Pacific region.
“I deeply value the commitment of these technology companies and welcome them to the Fostering the Future Together movement as we scale across continents,” said First Lady Melania Trump.
About Fostering the Future Together:Fostering the Future Together is a global coalition of nations unified to empower children through technology and education.
First Lady Melania Trump announced Fostering the Future Together during the 80th United Nations General Assembly. In spring 2026, she convened the initiative’s two-day meeting in Washington DC, bringing together First Spouses and technology-sector leaders at the United Sates Department of State. The gathering culminated at the White House, where the First Lady welcomed the largest assembly of First Spouses ever convened there for diplomatic purposes in U.S. history. During the 81st United Nations General Assembly, First Lady Melania Trump unveiled several new 2026 Fostering the Future Together regional events, including the G20 (USA), the ASEAN Conference (Philippines), Europe (Poland), and the Caribbean (Saint Kitts and Nevis).

The White HouseOctober 2, 2026
During National Breast Cancer Awareness Month, we celebrate the resilience and courage of our Nation’s four million breast cancer survivors, extend our unwavering support to those currently in the fight, and honor the memory of beloved family members and friends lost to this terrible disease.
In an instant, a breast cancer diagnosis forever changes the life of the patient and the lives of those around them. This year in the United States, more than 380,000 women will receive this devastating news, and approximately 40,000 souls will be lost to breast cancer. Thanks to medical breakthroughs, increased public awareness, and early detection, survival rates have drastically improved—but these numbers represent shattered lives and families, and that is unacceptable.
Through our historic mission to Make America Healthy Again, my Administration is committed to conquering chronic illness and advancing cutting-edge research, treatment options, and innovative therapies that will enhance the quality of life for men and women battling breast cancer and other diseases. Under my leadership, we will never stop working to deliver the breakthroughs, treatments, and cures that American patients and families deserve.
Breast cancer has caused immeasurable pain, fear, and uncertainty on too many American families, and throughout this month, we stand in compassionate solidarity with all cancer warriors. The First Lady and I encourage every person to know their family medical history and risk factors and to become a fierce advocate for their own health. May God comfort those who mourn, give strength to those suffering, and offer grace to the caregivers as we anticipate, with hope and confidence, the day this horrific disease is defeated once and for all.

item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National Domestic Violence Awareness MonthThe White HouseOctober 2, 2026

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 2, 2026
In communities across our great Nation, domestic violence destroys families, harms innocent children, and leaves lasting pain in our neighborhoods. For America to be strong, children must feel safe in their homes, spouses and significant others must be respected, and it must be a universal truth that violence in any form is unacceptable. This National Domestic Violence Awareness Month, my Administration reaffirms its commitment to permanently ending domestic violence and ensuring every American can live free from the threat of violence.
For as many as 10 million Americans, the unrelenting fear of violence in our homes, places of work, and other social settings make it impossible to enjoy life and foster healthy relationships. Behind every one of these numbers is a fellow American robbed of the safety and peace that our Nation promises to all its people. As President, I will always uplift survivors of domestic violence and make certain that shelters, counselors, advocates, and hotlines have the resources they need to answer each and every call for help. Help is always within reach, and you are never alone. If you are in need of immediate and confidential support, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233.
This month, we commit that for our mothers, our fathers, our daughters, and our sons, we will end the scourge of domestic violence. My Administration remains steadfast in safeguarding the safety and security of the American People, giving law enforcement the tools and resources they need to prevent domestic violence, and ensuring that those who commit acts of violence are held accountable. Together, we will protect the innocent, defend the vulnerable, and build a safer and stronger America.

item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National Cybersecurity Awareness MonthThe White HouseOctober 2, 2026

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 2, 2026
In an age of rapid digital advancement, cyberspace has emerged as the new frontier of American innovation, prosperity, and strength. As new technologies open doors to discovery and opportunity that were once unimaginable, a secure cyberspace is essential to ensuring that America continues to lead the world in finance, military power, emerging technology, and manufacturing. During National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, my Administration reaffirms our dedication to bolstering our Nation’s cybersecurity, protecting the American People, and unleashing the Golden Age of Cyberspace.
Every American relies on the digital world for information, economic opportunity, and the simple routines of daily life. Freedom and security in cyberspace, however, can never be taken for granted. For too long, adversaries and cybercriminals exploited our connected way of life to target our citizens, communities, and businesses without consequence. My Administration has put an end to this era of weakness.
As President, I signed an Executive Order to combat cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes and stop foreign criminal networks from preying on vulnerable Americans. In March, I released my Cyber Strategy for America—a bold vision for the future of American cybersecurity and innovation. My Administration is already putting this strategy into action through the creation of “GOLD EAGLE,” a partnership between the Federal Government and leading American companies to harness the power of American Super Intelligence to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities at rapid speed and stay ahead of our adversaries, defend the American People from emerging threats, and safeguard the critical infrastructure vital to our national security and global competitiveness.
As we secure America’s digital future, we are also preparing the next generation to lead it. Through First Lady Melania Trump’s leadership on the Presidential Super Intelligence Challenge, we have inspired young Americans to embrace emerging technologies, develop new skills, and find solutions to challenges in their own communities. The First Lady’s Fostering the Future Together initiative also continues to empower students, parents, and educators to learn, grow, and thrive through the safe and innovative use of advanced technology. This month, I encourage every American to do their own part to stay safe online by creating strong passwords, keeping software up to date, and remaining vigilant against scams. Together, we can strengthen our Nation’s cybersecurity, safeguard the technologies that power our daily lives, and secure America’s place as the leader in the world’s digital age.

item.title: Presidential Message on Down Syndrome Awareness Month
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Down Syndrome Awareness MonthThe White HouseOctober 2, 2026

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 2, 2026
Every child is a gift from God, created in His image and likeness, bringing hope, love, and a future filled with promise to our Nation and the world. This Down Syndrome Awareness Month, I join millions of Americans in celebrating the lives, accomplishments, and contributions of people with Down syndrome and honor the families and communities who stand beside them each and every day.
Americans with Down syndrome enrich every life they touch, meeting the world with a sincerity and joy that make our classrooms brighter and our communities stronger. Their condition arises from a single extra chromosome, a small difference that can slow a child’s development and bring challenges to families who love and care for them. In recent decades, our Nation’s doctors and researchers have answered these challenges with remarkable scientific discoveries, and in so doing have greatly enhanced the quality of life for children and adults living with Down syndrome.
As President, I have taken action to protect every innocent life and empower young Americans, including those living with Down syndrome, to lead long, productive, and fulfilling lives. My Administration is leading the charge, advancing the research that delivers new treatments and opening every door for these individuals to pursue their dreams and thrive in their communities. The families, friends, and caregivers who pour their hearts into looking after children with developmental disabilities are some of the most extraordinary, caring, and generous Americans—ensuring the more than 5,000 babies born with Down syndrome every year can live their American Dream just like every other citizen.
My Administration will never waver in our devotion to the men, women, and children living with Down syndrome, and I will always fight to ensure that they, like every other American, can be proud to live in a country with a government and a society that upholds the dignity of every precious life and recognizes the beauty and humanity of every person. This month, and every month, we celebrate, love, and cherish the incredible Americans living with Down syndrome.

The White HouseOctober 5, 2026
During Fire Prevention Week, my Administration honors the memory of America’s courageous firefighters and first responders for their extraordinary service and sacrifice. We are reaffirming our commitment to strengthening fire prevention and emergency response across the Nation. I encourage every American to take simple steps to protect their homes, families, and communities from preventable fires.
Fire safety begins at home. Every family can take precautions to prevent fires, and to better protect themselves and their loved ones. These can include mapping out a home escape plan, testing smoke and carbon monoxide alarms every month, replacing the worn wiring and overloaded outlets that spark so many household fires, or practicing safe charging habits that minimize the potential of fires from ubiquitous electronic devices. These commonsense steps can save lives by preventing fire or by ensuring families are prepared in the event of an emergency.
My Administration remains committed to protecting American lives from the threat of fires and improving our country’s ability to prevent and respond to them. Last year, I signed an Executive Order to streamline Federal wildfire response, strengthen local preparedness, and put modern technology to work detecting and fighting fires. We are also working to establish the United States Wildland Fire Service to better coordinate Federal wildfire programs and respond more effectively when fires break out.
This week, we also honor America’s extraordinary firefighters, first responders, emergency personnel, and volunteers who selflessly respond whenever the alarm sounds. Their determination to aid fellow Americans in distress embodies the highest American ideals of heroism, courage, and service to others. Together, we recommit to preventing fires, protecting our communities, and building a Nation more prepared, more ready, and more resilient than ever before.

item.title: Presidential Message on Child Health Day
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Child Health DayThe White HouseOctober 5, 2026

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 5, 2026
This Child Health Day, we renew our commitment to ensure the health and well-being of America’s children – our Nation’s future – so that they may live full, lasting, and happy lives free from the burden of health concerns.
As our children grow, we must protect their health and give them every opportunity to thrive. American children now face chronic health conditions and serious medical issues at rates far higher than in previous generations. With little explanation, we have witnessed sharp rises in the prevalence of obesity, diabetes, severe allergies, autism, autoimmune diseases, and mental health challenges such as anxiety and depression in our Nation’s youth. As President, I have a solemn duty to safeguard the health of the coming generation, and I will not rest until these conditions are understood and defeated and every child in America can grow up strong and whole.
For this reason, my Administration is confronting the chronic health crisis plaguing our Nation’s most vulnerable citizens by reversing the failed policies that have fueled America’s childhood disease epidemic and ensuring parents are informed with the Gold Standard Science to make the decisions for their children. Through the Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy—an initiative launched by the Make America Healthy Again Commission—we have taken over 120 specific actions to halt the rise in childhood chronic diseases and discover the root causes of serious medical conditions by improving preventative care, getting artificial dyes out of our food, accelerating breakthroughs and cures, and encouraging physical activity and limited screen time for children.
While more work remains to fully reverse these concerning trends, in just the first year of my Administration, we experienced the lowest death rate in recorded in our country’s history. Our Nation’s future relies upon the health and leadership of the next generation, which is why I remain committed to ensuring that Americans and their children receive the best medical advice to keep them healthy and the best care in the world if they do get sick. Under my leadership, we are delivering a healthcare system that restores trust and truly puts the health of children and families first, and together, we will make American children healthy again for generations to come.

item.title: Presidential Message on German American Day
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on German American DayThe White HouseOctober 6, 2026

Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on German American DayThe White HouseOctober 6, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 6, 2026
The German American story began on October 6, 1683, when 13 families from Krefeld, after braving the Atlantic in search of opportunity, landed on our shores and soon founded Germantown, Pennsylvania—the first permanent German settlement in America.
In the centuries since, German Americans have farmed the fields of our heartland and powered the industries that turned our young country into the mightiest economic powerhouse in the world.Their sons and daughters have defended American freedom in every era, serving valiantly in both World Wars and standing watch through the long struggle against communism during the Cold War. In our own time, their descendants continuetoserve in our Armed Forces, work the factories and family farms that sustain our Nation, and lead the businesses and communities that keep the American Dream alive for all of our citizens.
This spirit endures in the long-standing relationship between the United States and Germany—a relationship sustained by our mutual respect, and a shared desire for peace and prosperity. As President, I have led a historic renewal of the NATO alliance, securing a historic commitment from our NATO allies to increase their investment in our common defense. Since that historic summit in The Hague last year, Germany has taken bold steps toward the realization of a stronger, more balanced NATO. The impact of this commitment will be felt beyond Europe, as billions of dollars in new investments strengthen the transatlantic defense industrial base and create thousands of high-paying jobs for American workers.
Today, we give thanks for the generations of German Americans whose labor and love of liberty helped make the United States the greatest Nation on Earth. Their story is woven into the fabric of America, and together, we commit ourselves to building on this legacy to create an even brighter, more prosperous future for all Americans.
